extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate / beginning graduate students and instructors in differential equations and dynamical systems
extracted.subtask_description: Study and model the Lorenz system (and related mechanical explorations) including deriving equations, analyzing equilibria and stability, constructing Poincaré maps and a geometric model for the Lorenz attractor, and proving attractor properties (compactness, invariance, transitivity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservative system and potential energy (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the anisotropic Kepler system is conservative with potential energy U(x,y) = -1/√(µ x^2 + y^2); write down an explicit formula for total energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the given vector field to identify a potential function and form the total energy K+U. (System given earlier with parameter µ>1.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry of negative-energy surface (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the geometry of the energy surface Σ_h for energy h < 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterize the level set of the total energy in configuration/momentum space for negative total energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterize straight-line collision–ejection orbits (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restricting to negative energy, show that the only solutions that meet the zero velocity curve and are straight-line collision–ejection orbits lie on the x- and y-axes in configuration space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use symmetry and the zero-velocity curve to deduce which straight-line motions produce collision–ejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angular momentum not conserved (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that angular momentum is no longer an integral for this anisotropic system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the time derivative of angular momentum and demonstrate it is not zero in general when µ ≠ 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polar coordinate formulation (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewrite the anisotropic Kepler system in polar coordinates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Express x,y, velocities in r,θ and derive the r′, θ′ equations to analyze radial/angular behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blow-up of singularity via rescaling (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using a change of variables and time rescaling as in the Newtonian central force problem, blow up the singularity and write a new non-singular system at r=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard time rescaling and coordinate blow-up techniques to remove the r=0 singularity and obtain a regularized system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe collision surface geometry (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the structure of the collision surface (intersection of Σ_h with r=0 in scaled coordinates); justify calling it a 'bumpy torus.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze the scaled coordinates and show how the surface's topology/geometry leads to the 'bumpy torus' description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equilibria on collision surface and linearization (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find all equilibrium points on the collision surface and determine eigenvalues of the linearized system; classify which are sinks, sources, and saddles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute equilibria in the blown-up system on r=0 and linearize to classify stability via eigenvalues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bifurcation at µ = 9/8 (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the bifurcation that occurs on the collision surface when µ = 9/8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the parameter value where stability/type of equilibria change and describe the qualitative change in dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monotone function on collision surface (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a function that is nondecreasing along all non-equilibrium solutions in the collision surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a Lyapunov-type (or monotone) function on the collision surface showing monotonicity along orbits (helps rule out recurrence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fate of stable/unstable manifolds on collision surface (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the fate of the stable and unstable curves of the saddle points in the collision surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewrite the equation on the collision surface to eliminate time and estimate slopes as solutions climb the surface (hint given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative collision behavior for µ > 9/8 (anisotropic Kepler)
rubrics_metrics.description: When µ > 9/8, describe qualitatively how solutions that approach collision near the x-axis retreat from the origin in configuration space and how solutions approach collision near the y-axis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare dynamics near the two axes and describe asymmetry introduced by µ>1; characterize approaches/retreats qualitatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive glider motion equations from drag/lift assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Assuming drag and lift ∝ v^2, use Newton’s second law to derive the system governing a glider: θ′ = (v^2 − cos θ)/v, v′ = −sin θ − D v^2 (with D≥0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model forces parallel/perpendicular to velocity, project Newton's law onto θ and speed components to get the two-dimensional ODE system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find and classify equilibria of glider system
rubrics_metrics.description: Find all equilibrium solutions of the glider system and use linearization to determine their types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve for stationary (v,θ) and compute Jacobian/eigenvalues to classify stability (sinks/sources/saddles/centers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conserved quantity when D = 0 (glider)
rubrics_metrics.description: When D = 0, show that v^3 − 3v cos θ is constant along solution curves; sketch the phase plane and describe the xy-plane motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find first integral for D=0, use level curves to sketch phase portrait and relate orbits to motion in physical plane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of positive drag D on glider motion
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe what happens to the glider dynamics when D becomes positive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how dissipation (D>0) changes equilibrium/stability and long-term motion qualitatively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide conservativeness of given vector fields (exercise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine which of F(x,y) = (−x^2, −2y^2), F(x,y) = (x^2 − y^2, 2xy), F(x,y) = (x,0) on R^2 are conservative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check curl / existence of potential; test path-independence of line integrals or compute ∂F1/∂y = ∂F2/∂x conditions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conic section classification from polar equation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that 1/r = (1/h)(1 + e cos θ) determines hyperbola/parabola/ellipse when e>1, e=1, e<1 respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manipulate polar equation to standard conic forms and link eccentricity parameter to conic type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exact solution for particle moving radially outward (central force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider a particle initially moving directly away from origin in Newtonian central force; find explicit formula and discuss motion and reversal conditions for initial data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solve radial ODE for central potential and analyze turning points using energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometry of energy surface Σ_h for Newtonian central force
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the geometry of Σ_h for h>0 and h=0 in the Newtonian central force system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify energy level sets (unbounded, parabolic separatrix, bounded) in phase/configuration space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Path-independence implies conservative (work integral)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove that a force field F on R^3 is conservative iff the work integral along any path depends only on endpoints; if F = −grad V then work = V(X1) − V(X0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gradient theorem and show closed-loop integrals vanish for gradients; vice versa reconstruct potential from path integrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe solutions for non-Newtonian central force X'' = -X/|X|^4
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and describe solutions to X'' = -X/|X|^4.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use energy/angular momentum reduction or radial-equation techniques to determine qualitative motion (e.g., strong singular attraction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze repulsive inverse-cubic force X'' = X/|X|^3
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss solutions of X'' = X/|X|^3, noting this corresponds to a repulsive force at the origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study radial dynamics under repulsive singular potential and deduce escape/deflection behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-body problem equations from potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that the two-body equations can be written m_j X_j'' = -grad_j(U) when U = -g m1 m2 / |X2 − X1| (or equivalent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate potential with respect to each coordinate to get the force on each body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of total energy in two-body problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Show total energy K + U is constant of motion where K = 1/2 (m1|V1|^2 + m2|V2|^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate K+U along solutions and use equations of motion to show time derivative vanishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angular momentum first integral for two-body system
rubrics_metrics.description: Define angular momentum Λ = m1(X1 × V1) + m2(X2 × V2) and show Λ is a first integral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate Λ and use Newton's third law / central nature of forces to show derivative zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an attractor (compact & invariant)
rubrics_metrics.description: An attractor A for a flow is a set that is compact and invariant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the first of three formal conditions in the textbook definition of attractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an attractor (basin and forward intersection)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an open set U containing A such that φ_t(U) ⊂ U for t ≥ 0 and ⋂_{t≥0} φ_t(U) = A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition formalizes that A attracts all points of some neighborhood U and is the ω-limit intersection of forward images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of an attractor (transitivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitivity: For any points Y1,Y2 in A and neighborhoods U1,U2 in U, there exists a solution curve beginning in U1 that later passes through U2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This excludes decomposable sets (multiple dynamically distinct attractors) and ensures A is a single, transitive attractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of transitivity to rule out multiple attractors
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitivity condition rules out sets that meet (1) and (2) but are dynamically disconnected (e.g., an interval that contains two distinct sinks).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example given: planar system with two sinks shows the need for transitivity to consider a set a single attractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parameter constraints for Lorenz system analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Lorenz system parameters assumed positive with σ > b + 1; particular historic parameter choice σ=10, b=8/3, r=28 yields the classical chaotic case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parameter constraints are prerequisites used throughout the analysis (bifurcations, eigenvalue signs, existence of Q±).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liapunov function method to show global attraction for r<1
rubrics_metrics.description: For r<1, construct L(x,y,z)=x^2 + σ y^2 + σ z^2 and show ˙L<0 away from origin (via positivity of g(x,y)=x^2 + y^2 −(1+r)xy), proving origin is globally attracting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use strict Lyapunov function arguments to establish global stability of the origin when parameter r<1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipsoid trapping (existence of bounded attracting region)
rubrics_metrics.description: There exists ν* such that any solution starting outside the ellipsoid V(x,y,z)=ν* eventually enters this ellipsoid and remains trapped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose V(x,y,z)=r x^2 + σ y^2 + σ (z−2r)^2, compute ˙V and pick ν* so ˙V<0 outside inner ellipsoid (establishes bounded absorbing set).

rubrics_metrics.name: Divergence test for volume contraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute divergence div F = −(σ + 1 + b) (constant negative) to conclude volumes shrink exponentially; thus the attractor set has zero volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Liouville's theorem: dV/dt = ∫_D(t) div F and solve to show V(t) = e^{−(σ+1+b)t} V(0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Model return condition for Poincaré map (Guckenheimer–Williams model)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return condition: solutions through Σ_± (parts of plane Σ with y ≷ 0) return to Σ in forward time, yielding a Poincaré map Φ: Σ_+ ∪ Σ_- → Σ with symmetric property Φ(x,y) = −Φ(−x,−y).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assumption allows construction of a discrete return map that captures flow near equilibria and unstable branches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting direction hypothesis for Poincaré map
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting direction: For each fixed y≠0, Φ maps the line y=const into the line y=g(y) and contracts in the x-direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative form: 0 < ∂f/∂x < c < 1, ensuring contraction along x for map Φ(x,y) = (f(x,y), g(y)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expanding direction hypothesis for Poincaré map
rubrics_metrics.description: Expanding direction: Φ stretches Σ_± in y-direction by factor greater than √2, so g′(y) > √2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expansion combined with x-contraction produces the horseshoe-like folding mechanism crucial for chaotic dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbolicity condition for Poincaré map
rubrics_metrics.description: Hyperbolicity: DΦ maps tangent vectors with slopes ±1 to vectors with slopes of magnitude larger than μ>1 (sectors with |y|≥|x| mapped inside steeper-slope sectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures uniform expansion/contraction directions so that invariant set has hyperbolic structure (holds if |∂f/∂y| and c are sufficiently small).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytic form of Poincaré map
rubrics_metrics.description: Under assumptions the Poincaré map has the form Φ(x,y) = (f(x,y), g(y)) with contraction in x and expansion in y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This skew-product structure implies the one-dimensional map g on y essentially determines the dynamics on the attractor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tip behavior and singular limit of g
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical behavior: Φ(x,0) is undefined but lim_{y→0±} Φ(x,y) = ρ_± (tips); eigenvalue assumptions imply g(y) → ±∞ as y → 0±.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This accounts for folding that sends small-y strips to near tips, producing the characteristic map discontinuity at 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict Poincaré map to rectangle R and define attractor A
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrict attention to rectangle R (|y| ≤ y*) and define A = closure of ⋂_{n≥0} Φ^n(R) (then extend to flow attractor by taking flow of A and including origin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This construction isolates the compact invariant set (intersection of iterates) that corresponds to the attractor in the flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma: y-length growth under Φ
rubrics_metrics.description: For any open W ⊂ R, there exists n>0 such that the y-projection of Φ^n(W) equals the full interval (−y*, y*); equivalently Φ^n(W) meets each line y=c in interior of R.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the >√2 expansion in y and contraction properties to show y-length of connected pieces grows without bound under iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitivity proof strategy for Φ (showing A is attractor)
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove transitivity (thus A is an attractor), use contraction in x to make images close, the lemma to obtain any y-value, and choose iterates to map neighborhoods into each other within prescribed tolerance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative estimates: pick m with 40 c^m < diameter(W2) and use y-length growth to align y-coordinates, then contraction in x ensures closeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to one-dimensional dynamics (g determines attractor)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Φ maps vertical lines y=const to vertical lines and contracts x, the long-term dynamics on A are determined by the one-dimensional map g on I=[−y*,y*] (except y=0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studying iteration of g (forward and backward orbits) captures orbit structure on the attractor; points near same y coordinate collapse in x under iteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of preimages and orbit tree for g
rubrics_metrics.description: Points in interval [g(−y*), g(y*)] have two preimages, others have one; backward orbits are generally non-unique (binary tree of preimages) except for endpoints ±y*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This combinatorial branching is key to symbolic dynamics and constructing chaotic invariant sets (horseshoe-like behavior).
